title: Massachusetts Pharmacy Change Filings: Name, Ownership, Manager, Remodel, Relocation
topic: Pharmacy licensure / Changes to an already licensed pharmacy
subtopic: Which changes need prior Board approval, which need notice, on what clock and from whom, the two suitability screens behind a change of owner and a change of Manager of Record, and the federal registration steps that run alongside
learning_objectives: Sort a change to an operating pharmacy into the prior-approval family or the notice family before reaching for any number, and recognise the change of Manager of Record as belonging to both.

State the clock attached to each change and say which direction it runs: 14 days forward in 247 CMR 6.12, 14 days backward on each side of 247 CMR 6.11, 14 days backward in 247 CMR 6.14(1), 14 calendar days forward in 247 CMR 20.05, 30 days forward in 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) and 247 CMR 20.07(2), and 90 days backward in 247 CMR 6.16.
Identify the three express prohibitions on acting before the Board approves, in 247 CMR 6.15(1), 247 CMR 6.15(2) and 247 CMR 6.16.
Name who owes each filing, including the departing Manager of Record's own notice and the outgoing licensee's controlled-substance duties on a sale.
List what each application must carry, distinguishing the relocation drawings, the 247 CMR 6.15(3) remodeling drawings and the certified compounding blueprints in 247 CMR 6.15(4).
Explain how the 247 CMR 6.03 suitability factors reach beyond the named applicant and beyond Massachusetts pharmacies, and why a change of Manager of Record is screened under 247 CMR 6.10(3) instead.
Trace the federal registration steps that run beside a Massachusetts change: 21 CFR 1301.52 on a sale or a closure, and 21 CFR 1301.51 on a new name or address.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts pharmacy licence is not a general permission to operate; it describes one particular pharmacy, trading under a stated name, owned by a stated licensee, managed by a named Manager of Record, occupying a described footprint at a stated address. Every requirement in this section follows from that. When one of those facts changes, the licence on file stops describing the pharmacy that actually exists, and the regulations require the licensee either to tell the Board what happened or to ask the Board first. The whole topic is learned by asking, of any change, which of those two the Board demands, and the answer is not intuitive: a rebrand that changes nothing physical still generates a filing, while a move of two doors along cannot lawfully happen at all until the Board says yes.

The prior-approval family is defined by a prohibition rather than by a deadline, and 247 CMR 6.00 states three of them. Under 247 CMR 6.16 a pharmacy licensed by the Board shall apply for approval to relocate to a new address prior to relocating and may not relocate until it receives approval, and its application goes in at least 90 days before the desired date of relocation unless otherwise approved by the Board. Under 247 CMR 6.15(1) the listed pharmacy types shall apply for approval to remodel or to change the configuration or square footage and may not commence any construction work or remodeling until approval arrives. Under 247 CMR 6.15(2) a sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy shall apply for approval before moving, adding, modifying, removing or replacing any secondary engineering control, and may not do any of those things until approval arrives. In each the sanctionable act is moving, breaking ground or touching the engineering control, so filing the application authorises nothing; and of the three only 247 CMR 6.16 attaches a day count to the filing itself.

The notice family carries the numbers, and they do not all run the same way. 247 CMR 6.12 is titled Notifications, but the only change it reaches is the operating name: a licensee shall notify the Board, within 14 days, in writing, of any change in the name under which the pharmacy operates, accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation, so that clock starts at the change and runs forward. 247 CMR 6.11(1) runs the other way: at least 14 days prior to the transfer of ownership of a licensed pharmacy the licensee shall notify the Board of the proposed transfer, so the deadline sits in the past by the time the sale closes, and 247 CMR 6.11(2) puts the proposed new licensee's own application on the same backward count. The change of Manager of Record is the one candidates misread. 247 CMR 6.10(1) requires the pharmacy to submit an application to the Board for approval whenever there is a change of Manager of Record and states no day count of its own, but 247 CMR 20.05(1) supplies one: a pharmacy located in Massachusetts shall notify the Board within 14 calendar days of the resignation, termination, or change of its Manager of Record, and an application for change of Manager of Record shall satisfy that requirement.

Read 247 CMR 20.05 beside 247 CMR 6.10 and the shape of the duty changes. Because the 14 calendar days run forward from the resignation, termination or change, the change-of-Manager-of-Record application is a filing about something that has usually already happened: the manager may have died, fallen seriously ill or been terminated before anyone reaches for a form, and nothing in 247 CMR 6.10 bars the change from taking effect first. The one application is therefore both the request for approval and the report. It does not stand alone either. Under 247 CMR 20.05(3) a Manager of Record shall notify the Board of his or her resignation or termination as Manager of Record within 14 calendar days, a personal duty that the employer's filing does not discharge. And at some pharmacies a second, longer clock follows: under 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) the Manager of Record of a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy files a report within 30 days after any transfer of ownership or change in corporate officers, management personnel or Manager of Record, and 247 CMR 20.07(2) puts a non-resident pharmacy on the same 30 days.

Behind the paperwork sit two things the Board is protecting. The first is who stands behind the pharmacy, and there are two separate screens for it. On a transfer of ownership 247 CMR 6.11(4) lets the Board find the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the eleven factors in 247 CMR 6.03, which are framed as reaching an applicant, licensee, or interest holder, count conduct at any pharmacy, healthcare facility or other entity registered by the FDA or the DEA, include having prescriptive privileges as a listed status rather than a form of misconduct, and include discipline of, or a consent agreement on, the person's own professional licence or registration. On a change of Manager of Record the screen is 247 CMR 6.10(3) instead: a different list of ten factors, every one of them about the proposed Manager of Record, which adds discipline by the Board within five years of the date of the application and carries no prescriptive-privileges factor at all. The second thing protected is the controlled substance stock, which is why 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a) requires a dual-signed inventory attestation and 247 CMR 6.11(3) requires the buyer's application to carry a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances together with the inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14.

That last cross-reference is the one a reader skips past. The second sentence of 247 CMR 6.11(1) is that the outgoing licensee shall comply with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances, so the seller's obligations do not stop at the notice of the proposed transfer; and the provision that actually governs the stock is 247 CMR 6.14, headed Distribution of Controlled Substances upon Closure or Transfer of Ownership, whose inventory report 247 CMR 6.11(3) then demands of the buyer. Moving the stock therefore carries a certified written notice to the Board at least 14 days before the intended transfer, a bar on transferring sooner than 14 days after that notification, a transfer-date inventory signed by both Managers of Record, an attestation from both pharmacies within ten days of the transfer, readily retrievable copies kept for at least two years, and a prohibition on the transferor possessing any controlled substances afterwards. Running beside all of it is federal law, because 21 CFR 1301.52 governs the DEA registration on a sale or a discontinuance and 21 CFR 1301.51 governs its modification for a new name or address.

comparison_tables.title: What each filing must carry, and the item that distinguishes it

cells: Name change notice, 247 CMR 6.12
Written notice to the Board accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation
The authorizing documentation. A bare letter is not the notice the section describes
Relocation application, 247 CMR 6.16
An application with payment of the appropriate fee; blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout; any other information the Board requires
Nothing extra: the relocation drawings depict the layout, and 247 CMR 6.16 asks for neither the counseling area nor a transport security plan
Application to change the configuration or square footage, 247 CMR 6.15(3)

Blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, the prescription area and the counseling area; a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation, if the pharmacy is located in Massachusetts; any other information the Board requires
The counseling area, and the written transport security plan
What a compounding pharmacy adds, 247 CMR 6.15(4)

In support of an application to remodel or to change the configuration or square footage, a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy also submits certified blueprints depicting the compounding areas and the location and ISO classification of each primary and secondary engineering control and the placement of containment hoods, as applicable; a containment strategy; an environmental monitoring plan, if applicable; a plan to re-certify primary and secondary engineering controls and containment hoods, if applicable; a continuity of care plan, if applicable; and any other information the Board requires
That 247 CMR 6.15(3) is not the whole filing for these four types, and that the blueprints here must be certified and must carry the ISO classification of each engineering control
Change of Manager of Record application, 247 CMR 6.10(2)
The inventory attestation signed by the outgoing and the proposed incoming Manager of Record; the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence; required fees; any additional information the Board requires
The original licence itself, and the second signature on the attestation
Incoming licensee's application on a transfer, 247 CMR 6.11(3)

A complete application under 247 CMR 6.04 and 6.05 through 6.09; a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances; an inventory report of controlled substances required by 247 CMR 6.14; an official bill of sale; any additional information the Board requires
The official bill of sale, and the description of how and when the controlled substances move

The name, address and telephone number of the transferor and of the transferee pharmacy; the pharmacy licence and controlled substances registration numbers of each; the name and pharmacist licence number of each Manager of Record; the date the transfer will take place; and the security procedures for the transfer
That this is a separate certified notice from the 247 CMR 6.11(1) notice of the proposed transfer of ownership, with its own 14 days

comparison_tables.title: The federal step that runs beside each Massachusetts change

cells: Change in the name under which the pharmacy operates
Written notice to the Board within 14 days with appropriate authorizing documentation (247 CMR 6.12)

A written request to the DEA Registration Unit to modify the registration, carrying the registrant's name, address and registration number as printed on the certificate of registration together with the new name; no fee is required (21 CFR 1301.51(a) and (c))
Relocation to a new address
An application for approval at least 90 days ahead, and no relocation until the Board approves (247 CMR 6.16)

The same modification request, giving the new address instead; if it is approved a new certificate of registration issues, which the registrant maintains with the old one until expiration (21 CFR 1301.51(a) and (c))
Whether the incoming owner inherits what the outgoing owner held
The proposed new licensee submits an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy of its own, which the Board may refuse (247 CMR 6.11(2), (3) and (4))

No registration or any authority conferred by it may be assigned or otherwise transferred except pursuant to the Administration's written consent, so the buyer needs its own DEA registration (21 CFR 1301.52(b))
Transfer of ownership where the controlled stock goes with the business
The 247 CMR 6.11(1) notice, the buyer's 247 CMR 6.11(2) application, and the 247 CMR 6.14 procedure with its certified notice, 14-day wait, dual-signed transfer-date inventory and ten-day attestation

At least 14 days' advance notice to the Special Agent in Charge, in person or by registered or certified mail with return receipt requested, unless that officer waives the period; a transfer-date inventory serving as the transferor's final and the transferee's initial inventory; order forms for any Schedule I or II substances; and the records passing to the transferee (21 CFR 1301.52(d) and (e))
Closing down instead of selling
The outgoing licensee complies with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances (247 CMR 6.11(1))

A registrant discontinuing business without transferring it returns its certificate of registration and any unexecuted order forms to the DEA Registration Unit for cancellation, and may dispose of the controlled substances in its possession in accordance with 21 CFR part 1317 (21 CFR 1301.52(c))

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy signs a lease on a larger unit in the same shopping centre and intends to move over a weekend six weeks from now. The district manager says the pharmacy will write to the Board within 14 days of the move, the way it did last year when the chain rebranded. What do the regulations actually require?
steps: Classify the change before reaching for a number. A move to a new address is governed by 247 CMR 6.16, which is an approval provision, not a notification provision.

Read the prohibition in 247 CMR 6.16: the pharmacy shall apply for approval prior to relocating and may not relocate until it receives approval from the Board. Six weeks of planning is irrelevant if approval has not arrived.
Read the lead time: the application is submitted at least 90 days prior to the desired date of relocation, unless otherwise approved by the Board. Six weeks is inside that minimum.

Check what the application carries: an application with payment of the appropriate fee, blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, and any other information the Board requires.

Trace where the 14-day idea came from. 247 CMR 6.12 sets 14 days for a change in the name under which the pharmacy operates, which is a different change under a different section, and it says nothing about premises.

Do not stop at the Board. A new address is also a modification of the pharmacy's DEA registration under 21 CFR 1301.51(a), made by written request to the DEA Registration Unit giving the registrant's name, address and registration number as printed on the certificate of registration together with the new address. No fee is required, and the new certificate is maintained with the old one until expiration.
worked_examples.resolution: The pharmacy must apply at least 90 days ahead and may not move until the Board approves, and it must separately ask the DEA to modify its registration for the new address. The error the scenario invites is borrowing the familiar 14-day notice clock from the name-change provision and treating a relocation as something to report after it has happened.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy is being sold, and the controlled stock is to go across to the buyer's pharmacy. Twenty days before the closing date the buyer submits a complete licence application with an inventory report and the bill of sale. The seller files nothing, reasoning that the buyer's application already tells the Board everything about the transaction and that the pharmacy licence and the DEA registration will simply follow the business across.
steps: Separate the two duties in 247 CMR 6.11. Paragraph (1) is owed by the licensee: at least 14 days prior to the transfer of ownership it shall notify the Board of the proposed transfer.

Paragraph (2) is owed by the proposed new licensee: at least 14 days prior to the transfer it shall submit an application for a license to operate a pharmacy. The buyer's timely filing satisfies its own duty and nothing else.

Read the rest of 247 CMR 6.11(1) as it is written: the outgoing licensee shall comply with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances. The seller's obligations therefore run past its notice into the closing provisions and into what happens to the drugs.

Follow the stock to the provision that governs it. 247 CMR 6.14 is headed Distribution of Controlled Substances upon Closure or Transfer of Ownership, and 247 CMR 6.11(3) makes its inventory report part of the buyer's own application. Moving the stock needs a certified written notice to the Board at least 14 days before the intended transfer, and the transfer may proceed no sooner than 14 days following that notification.

Work the rest of 247 CMR 6.14(2): a transfer-date inventory of all controlled substances in Schedules II through V and all Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program, signed by the pharmacist Manager of Record of each pharmacy; an attestation filed with the Board by both pharmacies within ten days of the transfer; readily retrievable copies kept for at least two years; and no controlled substances in the transferor's possession after the date of transfer.

Check the buyer's application against 247 CMR 6.11(3): a complete application, a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances, the inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14, the official bill of sale, and anything else the Board requires.

Notice what the buyer is actually asking for. This is an application the Board may refuse, and under 247 CMR 6.11(4) it may find the proposed new licensee or any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors.

Take the federal limb separately. Under 21 CFR 1301.52(b) no registration or any authority conferred by it may be assigned or otherwise transferred except pursuant to written consent, so the buyer needs a registration of its own; and under 21 CFR 1301.52(d) the transferor gives the Special Agent in Charge at least 14 days' advance notice of the proposed transfer, in person or by registered or certified mail with return receipt requested, unless that officer waives the period.
worked_examples.resolution: The seller's position is unsound on every limb. The errors are treating a sale as one transaction with one filing, assuming that a pharmacy licence and a DEA registration pass with the business, and forgetting that the controlled stock has a notice, a waiting period, an inventory and an attestation of its own on both sides of the border.

worked_examples.scenario: A Manager of Record is terminated on a Friday and refuses to return to the pharmacy. The owner wants a staff pharmacist to sign the inventory attestation in the departed manager's place, asks whether the inventory can be limited to Schedules II through V, and assumes that because 247 CMR 6.10 sets no deadline the change-of-Manager application can wait until a permanent replacement has been recruited.
steps: Start with the default in 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a): the attestation confirming the pharmacy performed an inventory and filed the report with its controlled substance records is signed by the outgoing Manager of Record and the proposed incoming Manager of Record.

Check whether the substitution route is open. A staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign only where the outgoing Manager is unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, and termination is one of the three listed grounds, so it is available here.
Attach the condition: the Board must be notified at the time the application is submitted of the reason the staff pharmacist is signing. The substitution is not silent.

Answer the scope question. The inventory covers all controlled substances in Schedules II through V and Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program, so limiting it to II through V is short.

Assemble the rest of the application under 247 CMR 6.10(2): the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence, the required fees, and any additional information the Board requires. Expect that the Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.

Now answer the deadline question, which 247 CMR 6.10 does not. Under 247 CMR 20.05(1) a pharmacy located in Massachusetts shall notify the Board within 14 calendar days of the resignation, termination, or change of its Manager of Record, and an application for change of Manager of Record shall satisfy that requirement. The 14 calendar days have been running since the Friday, and waiting out a recruitment process is not an option the regulation offers.

Add the duty that is not the pharmacy's at all. Under 247 CMR 20.05(3) the departed manager shall notify the Board of his or her own termination as Manager of Record within 14 calendar days, and the employer's filing does not discharge it.
worked_examples.resolution: The staff pharmacist may sign because termination is one of the three listed grounds, provided the reason is given to the Board with the application; the inventory must reach reportable Schedule VI; and the clock is already running under 247 CMR 20.05(1). The errors invited here are treating the substitution as generally available for an uncooperative manager, stopping the count at Schedule V, and reading silence in 247 CMR 6.10 as the absence of any deadline.

worked_examples.scenario: A Drug Store pharmacy is enlarging its prescription area by taking in an adjoining storeroom. The contractor is booked for Monday morning, and the pharmacy files its application first thing Monday, enclosing drawings of the enlarged prescription area. The owner reasons that the application is in and that work can stop if the Board objects, and asks what would be different if the same company's sterile compounding pharmacy did similar work that moved a cleanroom wall.
steps: Identify the provision. Taking in a storeroom changes both the configuration and the square footage, which is squarely within 247 CMR 6.15(1).

Read the prohibition rather than a deadline: the pharmacy may not commence any construction work or remodeling until it receives approval from the Board. Filing on Monday morning does not license Monday morning's work.

Test the drawings against 247 CMR 6.15(3)(a), which requires blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, the prescription area and the counseling area. Drawings of the prescription area alone are incomplete.
Add the Massachusetts-only item under 247 CMR 6.15(3)(b): a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation, required if the pharmacy is located in Massachusetts.

Turn to the sterile compounding pharmacy and read 247 CMR 6.15(4), which the Drug Store does not owe. A sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy also submits certified blueprints depicting the compounding areas and the location and ISO classification of each primary and secondary engineering control and the placement of containment hoods, a containment strategy, an environmental monitoring plan, a plan to re-certify primary and secondary engineering controls and containment hoods, and a continuity of care plan, each as applicable.

Then read 247 CMR 6.15(2), which is a second prohibition rather than a list. Moving a cleanroom wall may move, modify or replace a secondary engineering control, and a sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy shall apply for approval before doing any of those things and may not do them until approval arrives.

Compare all of this with a relocation application, which under 247 CMR 6.16 asks for the fee and drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, and calls for neither the counseling area nor the transport security plan.
worked_examples.resolution: For the Drug Store two things are wrong: work may not start before approval, and the drawings omit the counseling area, with the transport security plan missing as well. For the sterile compounding pharmacy a third appears, because 247 CMR 6.15(4) adds five specific submissions and 247 CMR 6.15(2) separately bars touching a secondary engineering control before the Board approves. The error the scenario invites is treating the act of filing as the trigger, so that a pending application feels like permission.

worked_examples.scenario: A company applying to take over a Massachusetts pharmacy has a minority investor whose previous out-of-state pharmacy entered a consent agreement resolving a complaint, and whose own separate professional licence was suspended some years ago. The same company proposes a new Manager of Record who was disciplined by the Board four years ago. Counsel advises that one list of factors answers both questions.
steps: Take the ownership limb first. Under 247 CMR 6.11(4) the Board may find the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the factors in 247 CMR 6.03, and those factors are framed as reaching an applicant, licensee, or interest holder, so the minority investor is inside the inquiry even though the company is the named applicant.

Check the out-of-state consent agreement. 247 CMR 6.03(5) lists a consent agreement in resolution of a complaint against a pharmacy, healthcare facility or other entity registered by the FDA or the DEA that the person owned, operated or held an interest in, resulting in disciplinary action, and nothing confines it to Massachusetts.

Check the suspended professional licence separately, because it is a different factor. 247 CMR 6.03(10) lists a professional license or registration of the person's own that was the subject of proceedings resulting in discipline, suspension, denial or revocation, and 247 CMR 6.03(11) adds a consent agreement resolving a complaint against such a licence.

Now take the manager limb, which is not on that list at all. 247 CMR 6.10(3) supplies the factors for a change-of-Manager-of-Record application, and 247 CMR 6.10(3)(h) lists a proposed Manager of Record who has been disciplined by the Board within five years of the date of the application, so four years ago falls inside it.

Note the two directions in which the lists diverge. 247 CMR 6.03(9) makes having prescriptive privileges a listed factor and 247 CMR 6.10(3) has no such item, while 247 CMR 6.10(3) reaches an entity the proposed Manager merely managed and carries the five-year Board-discipline factor that 247 CMR 6.03 does not.
worked_examples.resolution: Counsel is wrong: two applications sit in front of the Board and each has its own list. The investor's history is weighed under 247 CMR 6.03 even though the company is the named applicant, and the proposed Manager of Record is weighed under 247 CMR 6.10(3), where discipline by the Board within five years of the application is a factor in its own right.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A licensee shall notify the Board of a change in the name under which the pharmacy operates within ______, in ______, accompanied by ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 14 days; writing; appropriate authorizing documentation (247 CMR 6.12).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A relocation application must be submitted at least ______ before the desired date of relocation, unless ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 90 days; otherwise approved by the Board (247 CMR 6.16).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: On a transfer of ownership the licensee must notify the Board at least ______ before the transfer, and the proposed new licensee must submit its licence application at least ______ before the transfer.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 14 days; 14 days. It is the same period, owed independently by each side under 247 CMR 6.11(1) and (2).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which three changes carry an express prohibition on acting before the Board approves, and what is each prohibited from doing?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Relocation, where the pharmacy may not relocate until it receives approval (247 CMR 6.16); remodeling or a change of configuration or square footage, where the pharmacy may not commence any construction work or remodeling until it receives approval (247 CMR 6.15(1)); and a change to a secondary engineering control, where a sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy may not move, add, modify, remove or replace one until it receives approval (247 CMR 6.15(2)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Drawings submitted under 247 CMR 6.15(3)(a) must depict the pharmacy layout, the ______ area and the ______ area.
retrieval_prompts.answer: prescription; counseling.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which item does 247 CMR 6.15(3) require of a pharmacy located in Massachusetts that 247 CMR 6.16 does not ask of a relocating pharmacy?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Beyond the 247 CMR 6.15(3) items, name the five submissions 247 CMR 6.15(4) adds, and the four pharmacy types that owe them.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Certified blueprints depicting the compounding areas with the location and ISO classification of each primary and secondary engineering control and the placement of containment hoods; a containment strategy; an environmental monitoring plan; a plan to re-certify primary and secondary engineering controls and containment hoods; and a continuity of care plan, each as applicable. They are owed by a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The change of Manager of Record inventory attestation is normally signed by ______ and ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: the outgoing Manager of Record; the proposed incoming Manager of Record (247 CMR 6.10(2)(a)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign the inventory report only where the outgoing Manager of Record is unavailable due to ______, ______ or ______, and provided ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: death; serious illness; termination; the Board is notified at the time the application is submitted of the reason the staff pharmacist is signing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The inventory behind a change of Manager of Record covers all controlled substances in Schedules ______ and also ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: II through V; Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: 247 CMR 6.10 states no day count for a change of Manager of Record. Where does the clock come from, what is it, and what does it run from?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 247 CMR 20.05(1): a pharmacy located in Massachusetts notifies the Board within 14 calendar days of the resignation, termination, or change of its Manager of Record, and an application for change of Manager of Record satisfies that requirement. The period runs forward from the event, so the change has usually already happened.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which duty on a change of Manager of Record belongs to the departing manager personally, and by when?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Notice to the Board of his or her own resignation or termination as Manager of Record, within 14 calendar days (247 CMR 20.05(3)). The pharmacy's application does not discharge it.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which pharmacies file a report within 30 days after a transfer of ownership or a change of Manager of Record, and under which provisions?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Manager of Record of a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy under 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e), and a non-resident pharmacy under 247 CMR 20.07(2). Both also report annually, and a change in corporate officers or management personnel starts the same 30 days.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Besides the complete application, name the three items 247 CMR 6.11(3) requires from the proposed new licensee.
retrieval_prompts.answer: A description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances; an inventory report of controlled substances required by 247 CMR 6.14; and an official bill of sale.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does 247 CMR 6.11(1) require of the outgoing licensee besides notifying the Board of the proposed transfer, and what happens to the stock?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Compliance with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances. The stock itself moves under 247 CMR 6.14: certified notice at least 14 days before the intended transfer, no transfer sooner than 14 days after that notification, a transfer-date inventory signed by both Managers of Record, an attestation from both pharmacies within ten days, readily retrievable copies for at least two years, and no controlled substances left with the transferor.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The 247 CMR 6.03 suitability factors are framed as reaching an applicant, a licensee or ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: an interest holder.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which listed 247 CMR 6.03 factor is a status rather than a form of misconduct?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 247 CMR 6.03(9): that the applicant, licensee or interest holder has prescriptive privileges.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which two 247 CMR 6.03 factors turn on the person's own professional licence rather than on an entity the person was behind?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 247 CMR 6.03(10), a professional license or registration that was the subject of proceedings resulting in discipline, suspension, denial or revocation; and 247 CMR 6.03(11), a consent agreement in resolution of a complaint against a professional license or registration resulting in disciplinary action.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which list of factors governs a change-of-Manager-of-Record application, and name the factor it carries that 247 CMR 6.03 does not?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 247 CMR 6.10(3). It lists a proposed Manager of Record who has been disciplined by the Board within five years of the date of the application.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which changes to an operating pharmacy carry a filing requirement with no day count stated anywhere, and why is a change of Manager of Record not one of them?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Remodeling or a change of configuration or square footage, and a change to a secondary engineering control: 247 CMR 6.15 states no number and the controlling constraint is the prohibition on acting before approval. A change of Manager of Record is not an answer, because 247 CMR 20.05(1) supplies 14 calendar days.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A Massachusetts pharmacy changes its operating name. What does federal law require alongside the 247 CMR 6.12 notice?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A written request to the DEA Registration Unit to modify the registration under 21 CFR 1301.51(a), giving the registrant's name, address and registration number as printed on the certificate of registration together with the new name. No fee is required, and the new certificate of registration is maintained with the old one until expiration.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How far ahead, to whom and by what means must a registrant transferring its business with its controlled substances give federal notice, and what may shorten the period?
retrieval_prompts.answer: At least 14 days in advance of the proposed transfer, to the Special Agent in Charge in the registrant's area, in person or by registered or certified mail with return receipt requested. Only a waiver by the Special Agent in Charge shortens it (21 CFR 1301.52(d)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: On the date of a federal transfer of a business, what does the single inventory serve as, and which schedules still move on order forms?
retrieval_prompts.answer: It serves as the final inventory of the registrant-transferor and the initial inventory of the registrant-transferee, with a copy in each person's records. Schedule I and Schedule II substances still require order forms (21 CFR 1301.52(e)).

quick_review.text: 247 CMR 6.12 is headed Notifications, but the only change it reaches is the name under which the pharmacy operates: written notice to the Board within 14 days, with appropriate authorizing documentation.

A transfer of ownership generates two duties on the same backward 14-day count: the licensee notifies the Board of the proposed transfer, and the proposed new licensee submits an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy.

247 CMR 6.11(1) also sends the outgoing licensee to 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances, and the stock itself moves under 247 CMR 6.14.

The incoming licensee's application carries a complete application, a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances, the inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14, an official bill of sale, and anything else the Board requires.

247 CMR 6.14 has clocks of its own on a sale or a closure: certified notice at least 14 days before the intended transfer of Schedules II through VI, no transfer sooner than 14 days following the notification, a transfer-date inventory of Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI signed by both Managers of Record, an attestation from both pharmacies within ten days of the transfer, readily retrievable copies for at least two years, and no controlled substances left with the transferor.

A pharmacy may not relocate until it receives Board approval, and applies at least 90 days before the desired relocation date unless the Board approves otherwise, with the fee and drawings depicting the pharmacy layout.

A pharmacy may not commence any construction work or remodeling until the Board approves a remodel or a change of configuration or square footage; the drawings must show the layout, the prescription area and the counseling area.
A pharmacy located in Massachusetts also submits, with a 247 CMR 6.15(3) application, a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation.

247 CMR 6.15(2): a sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy must have Board approval before moving, adding, modifying, removing or replacing any secondary engineering control, and may not do so until it receives approval.

247 CMR 6.15(4): a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy adds certified blueprints carrying the ISO classification of each primary and secondary engineering control, a containment strategy, an environmental monitoring plan, a plan to re-certify the engineering controls and containment hoods, and a continuity of care plan, each as applicable.

A change of Manager of Record is an application to the Board for approval, carrying a dual-signed inventory attestation, the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence and the required fees; the Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.

247 CMR 20.05: a pharmacy located in Massachusetts notifies the Board within 14 calendar days of the resignation, termination, or change of its Manager of Record and the application for change satisfies that duty, while the departing Manager of Record owes a personal notice of his or her own resignation or termination within 14 calendar days.

247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) and 247 CMR 20.07(2): compounding pharmacies and non-resident pharmacies report annually and within 30 days after any transfer of ownership or change in corporate officers, management personnel or Manager of Record.

The 247 CMR 6.03 factors are the Board's discretionary grounds for concluding that licensing an applicant or licensee would not be in the interest of public health, safety and welfare, and they include both prescriptive privileges and discipline on the person's own professional licence.

247 CMR 6.10(3) supplies the Board's factors on a change-of-Manager-of-Record application, describing the proposed Manager of Record alone and adding discipline by the Board within five years of the date of the application.

21 CFR 1301.52(b): no DEA registration or any authority conferred by it may be assigned or otherwise transferred except pursuant to the Administration's written consent, so an incoming owner needs a registration of its own.

21 CFR 1301.51(a): a change of name or address is made by a written request to modify the existing DEA registration, with no fee, and the new certificate of registration is kept with the old one until expiration.

decision_logic.condition: A fact about an operating pharmacy is about to change, or has just changed.
decision_logic.action: Ask first whether the provision governing it is an approval provision or a notification provision, and only then look for a number. Relocation and remodeling are approvals, a name change is a notice, and a change of Manager of Record is both, because 247 CMR 6.10 requires an application for approval while 247 CMR 20.05(1) makes that application the 14-calendar-day report.

decision_logic.condition: The change is the name under which the pharmacy operates.
decision_logic.action: Notify the Board in writing within 14 days of the change and send the appropriate authorizing documentation with the notice, whether or not the licensee, the premises and the ownership are unchanged; then apply to modify the DEA registration for the new name under 21 CFR 1301.51(a).

File the licensee's own notice of the proposed transfer at least 14 days before it, confirm separately that the proposed new licensee has filed its own application at least 14 days before the transfer, and then work the outgoing licensee's remaining duties: the closing provisions 247 CMR 6.11(1) names, the 247 CMR 6.14 procedure for the stock, and the 21 CFR 1301.52(d) notice to the Special Agent in Charge. Do not let any one filing stand in for another.

decision_logic.condition: You are the incoming owner or the incoming Manager of Record.
decision_logic.action: Assemble the controlled substance paperwork the provisions name: the transfer description and 247 CMR 6.14 inventory report with the bill of sale for a change of owner, and the dual-signed inventory attestation with the original licence for a change of Manager.

decision_logic.condition: The outgoing Manager of Record will not or cannot sign the attestation.
decision_logic.action: Check the reason against the three listed grounds of death, serious illness and termination. If one applies, authorise a staff pharmacist and tell the Board the reason at the time the application is submitted; if none applies, the substitution is not open.

decision_logic.condition: The Manager of Record has resigned, been terminated or otherwise changed.
decision_logic.action: Start 14 calendar days running from that event under 247 CMR 20.05(1) and file the change-of-Manager application inside them, since the application satisfies the notice. Remind the departing manager of the separate personal notice in 247 CMR 20.05(3), and at a compounding or non-resident pharmacy diarise the 30-day report under 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) or 247 CMR 20.07(2).

decision_logic.condition: Construction, reconfiguration or a change of square footage is planned.
decision_logic.action: Stop work until approval arrives, and check the drawings for the counseling area as well as the layout and the prescription area, adding the written transport security plan for a pharmacy located in Massachusetts. If the pharmacy is a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy, add the 247 CMR 6.15(4) submissions as well.

decision_logic.condition: A secondary engineering control is to be moved, added, modified, removed or replaced.
decision_logic.action: Treat it as its own approval event under 247 CMR 6.15(2) for a sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy, and do none of those things until the Board approves.

decision_logic.condition: A move to a new address is planned.
decision_logic.action: Count back at least 90 days from the desired relocation date and file the application with the fee and layout drawings, do not relocate until the Board approves, and ask the DEA to modify the registration for the new address.

decision_logic.condition: The question asks what the Board may do with an application rather than what a licensee must file.
decision_logic.action: Ask which application first. For a licence application or a transfer of ownership the factors are in 247 CMR 6.03, which reach an interest holder as well as the applicant and count history at any FDA- or DEA-registered entity, and 247 CMR 6.11(4) applies them to the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder. For a change of Manager of Record the factors are in 247 CMR 6.10(3), which describe the proposed Manager alone and add discipline by the Board within five years of the application.

ma_vs_federal.text: These filings are Massachusetts licensure requirements in 247 CMR 6.00, but federal law is not confined to the suitability inquiry. Inside 247 CMR itself, 247 CMR 6.03 counts a person's history at a pharmacy, healthcare facility or other entity registered by the FDA or the DEA, so out-of-state and non-pharmacy federal registrants are inside a Massachusetts suitability question.

A sale carries DEA steps of its own. Under 21 CFR 1301.52(b) no registration or any authority conferred by it may be assigned or otherwise transferred except on conditions the Administration designates and only pursuant to written consent, so an incoming owner needs its own registration rather than the seller's. Under 21 CFR 1301.52(d) a registrant discontinuing business by transferring it, together with its controlled substances, submits to the Special Agent in Charge in its area, in person or by registered or certified mail with return receipt requested, at least 14 days in advance of the proposed transfer unless that officer waives the period, the details of transferor and transferee and the date the transfer will occur.

The federal transfer then has mechanics the Massachusetts procedure does not duplicate: a complete inventory on the date of transfer that serves as the transferor's final and the transferee's initial inventory, with a copy in each person's records; order forms for any Schedule I or II substances; and the records for the substances transferred passing to the transferee on that date. A registrant that discontinues without transferring the business instead returns its certificate of registration and any unexecuted order forms to the DEA Registration Unit for cancellation, and may dispose of the controlled substances in its possession in accordance with 21 CFR part 1317.

A change of name or address is federally a modification rather than a new registration. Under 21 CFR 1301.51(a) the registrant applies by written request to the DEA Registration Unit, giving its name, address and registration number as printed on the certificate of registration together with the new name or address, and under 21 CFR 1301.51(c) no fee is required, the request is handled in the same manner as an application for registration, and any new certificate is maintained with the old one until expiration.

Keep the two sets of controlled-substance paperwork apart. What 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a) and 247 CMR 6.11(3) require is Board-facing: the change-of-Manager inventory report is filed with the pharmacy's own controlled substance records and attested to the Board, and the transfer description and inventory report are components of a Board application. That is the Massachusetts side only, and satisfying it leaves the federal steps above still to be taken.

exceptions.text: The 90-day relocation lead time yields to the Board: 247 CMR 6.16 states it unless otherwise approved by the Board. The prohibition on relocating before approval carries no such qualifier.

The dual-signature attestation has exactly one substitution route: a staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign where the outgoing Manager of Record is unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, provided the Board is notified at the time of application of the reason.
The written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation is required under 247 CMR 6.15(3)(b) only if the pharmacy is located in Massachusetts.

The three lists in 247 CMR 6.15 are not the same. 247 CMR 6.15(1) reaches a Drug Store, sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy, and the only non-resident type on it is a non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy.

The other two lists narrow differently: 247 CMR 6.15(2) reaches only sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding and institutional sterile compounding pharmacies, while 247 CMR 6.15(4) reaches sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding and non-resident sterile compounding pharmacies. A complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy therefore owes the 247 CMR 6.15(4) submissions but is not named in 247 CMR 6.15(2).

Four of the 247 CMR 6.15(4) submissions are themselves qualified: the placement of containment hoods on the certified blueprints, the environmental monitoring plan, the plan to re-certify the engineering controls and containment hoods, and the continuity of care plan are each required as or if applicable.

The 14 calendar days in 247 CMR 20.05 carry no 'unless otherwise authorized' qualifier, and the regulation itself states that an application for change of Manager of Record satisfies the pharmacy's notice.

The 30-day report in 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) and 247 CMR 20.07(2) is triggered by a change in corporate officers or management personnel as well as by a transfer of ownership or a change of Manager of Record, and it is additional to the annual report in the same provisions.

The two 14-day periods on a transfer of the stock yield to different people: the Massachusetts period in 247 CMR 6.14(1) applies unless otherwise authorized by the Board, while the federal period in 21 CFR 1301.52(d) applies unless the Special Agent in Charge waives the time limitation in an individual instance.

timing_deadlines.event: Change in the name under which the pharmacy operates
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 14 days, in writing, running forward from the change
timing_deadlines.consequence: The notice must be accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation, so a bare letter does not discharge 247 CMR 6.12, and waiting for the next renewal is out of time.

timing_deadlines.event: Transfer of ownership, the licensee's notice
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the transfer
timing_deadlines.consequence: The clock runs backwards from the closing date and the duty is the outgoing licensee's own; the buyer's filing does not answer it.

timing_deadlines.event: Transfer of ownership, the proposed new licensee's application
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the transfer
timing_deadlines.consequence: This is an application to be granted rather than a notice to be logged: the Board may find the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors.

timing_deadlines.event: Certified notice of the controlled-substance transfer that accompanies a sale or a closure
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the intended transfer, unless otherwise authorized by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: The transfer may proceed no sooner than 14 days following the notification, so this notice starts a waiting period rather than merely meeting a deadline, and it is separate from the 247 CMR 6.11(1) notice of the proposed transfer of ownership.

timing_deadlines.event: Attestation confirming the controlled substance inventory on such a transfer
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within ten days of the transfer, filed by both pharmacies
timing_deadlines.consequence: It is counted from the transfer rather than from the notice, and ten days is not 14.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Application at least 90 days before the desired date of relocation, unless otherwise approved by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: The 90 days is a minimum lead time, not the whole duty: the pharmacy may not relocate until it receives approval.

timing_deadlines.event: Remodeling, or a change of configuration or square footage
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No day count is stated in 247 CMR 6.15
timing_deadlines.consequence: The controlling constraint is the prohibition instead: no construction work or remodeling may commence until the Board approves.

timing_deadlines.event: Moving, adding, modifying, removing or replacing a secondary engineering control
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No day count is stated in 247 CMR 6.15(2)
timing_deadlines.consequence: Again the constraint is a prohibition: the pharmacy may do none of those things until it receives approval from the Board.

timing_deadlines.event: Change of Manager of Record at a pharmacy located in Massachusetts
timing_deadlines.timeframe: 247 CMR 6.10 states no day count; 247 CMR 20.05(1) requires notice within 14 calendar days of the resignation, termination or change, and the change-of-Manager application satisfies it
timing_deadlines.consequence: The period runs forward from an event that has usually already occurred, and the filing is still an application for approval, so the Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it and may refuse it on the 247 CMR 6.10(3) factors.

timing_deadlines.event: Departing Manager of Record's own notice to the Board
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 14 calendar days of his or her resignation or termination as Manager of Record
timing_deadlines.consequence: The duty in 247 CMR 20.05(3) is personal to the individual, and the pharmacy's application does not answer it.

timing_deadlines.event: Report after a transfer of ownership or a change of Manager of Record at a compounding or non-resident pharmacy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 30 days after the transfer or change, and annually
timing_deadlines.consequence: It is owed under 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) and 247 CMR 20.07(2) and sits on top of the 14-calendar-day notice, so meeting one does not answer the other.

timing_deadlines.event: Federal notice of a transfer of the business together with its controlled substances
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days in advance of the proposed transfer, unless the Special Agent in Charge waives the time limitation
timing_deadlines.consequence: It goes to the Special Agent in Charge in the registrant's area, in person or by registered or certified mail with return receipt requested, and it is separate from every Massachusetts filing.

forms_records.text: Name change: written notice to the Board accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation.
Transfer of ownership, outgoing side: the notice of the proposed transfer, and compliance with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances.

Transfer of ownership, incoming side: a complete application under 247 CMR 6.04 and 6.05 through 6.09, a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances, an inventory report of controlled substances required by 247 CMR 6.14, an official bill of sale, and any additional information the Board requires.

Moving the stock: a 247 CMR 6.14(1) certified notice naming both pharmacies with address and telephone number, both pharmacy licence and controlled substances registration numbers, both Managers of Record with their pharmacist licence numbers, the date the transfer will take place and the security procedures for the transfer; then the inventory report signed by both Managers of Record and the attestation filed by both pharmacies.

Change of Manager of Record: an inventory attestation signed by the outgoing and the proposed incoming Manager of Record, the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence, required fees, and any additional information the Board requires. The application itself is signed by the licensee or its authorised representative and the proposed new Manager of Record.
The change of Manager of Record inventory report is filed with the pharmacy's own controlled substance records, and the attestation confirms to the Board that this was done.
Relocation: an application with payment of the appropriate fee, blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, and any other information the Board requires.

An application to change the configuration or square footage: blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, the prescription area and the counseling area; a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation for a pharmacy located in Massachusetts; and any other information the Board requires.

What a compounding pharmacy adds under 247 CMR 6.15(4): certified blueprints depicting the compounding areas and the location and ISO classification of each primary and secondary engineering control and the placement of containment hoods, a containment strategy, an environmental monitoring plan, a plan to re-certify primary and secondary engineering controls and containment hoods, a continuity of care plan, each as applicable, and any other information the Board requires.

Federal paperwork on a change: a written request to the DEA Registration Unit under 21 CFR 1301.51(a) for a new name or address, carrying the registrant's name, address and registration number as printed on the certificate of registration.

Federal paperwork on a discontinuance without a transfer: the certificate of registration and any unexecuted order forms returned to the DEA Registration Unit for cancellation under 21 CFR 1301.52(c).

role_duties.duty: Notify the Board in writing within 14 days of any change in the name under which the pharmacy operates, with appropriate authorizing documentation.

role_duties.role: Licensee, outgoing owner on a transfer
role_duties.duty: Notify the Board of the proposed transfer of ownership at least 14 days before it, and comply with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances.

role_duties.role: Transferor pharmacy moving its stock on a sale or a closure
role_duties.duty: Give the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before the intended transfer of Schedules II through VI, wait out the 14 days, take the transfer-date inventory, sign and file the ten-day attestation, keep a readily retrievable copy for at least two years, and possess no controlled substances after the date of transfer.

Submit an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy at least 14 days before the transfer, supported by the complete application, the controlled substance transfer description, the 247 CMR 6.14 inventory report and the official bill of sale.
Stand to be assessed on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors alongside the proposed new licensee, even though the interest holder is not the named applicant.

role_duties.role: Pharmacy located in Massachusetts on a change of Manager of Record
role_duties.duty: Notify the Board within 14 calendar days of the resignation, termination or change of its Manager of Record, which an application for change of Manager of Record satisfies.

Sign the attestation confirming the controlled substance inventory was performed and filed, unless unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination; and separately notify the Board of his or her own resignation or termination as Manager of Record within 14 calendar days.
Sign both the change of Manager of Record application and the inventory attestation, appear before the Board if it so requires, and stand to be assessed on the 247 CMR 6.10(3) factors.

role_duties.role: Manager of Record of a compounding pharmacy, and a non-resident pharmacy
role_duties.duty: File the report required within 30 days after any transfer of ownership or change in corporate officers, management personnel or Manager of Record, and annually.
Obtain Board approval before commencing any construction work or remodeling, and file drawings showing the layout, the prescription area and the counseling area.

role_duties.role: Sterile, non-resident sterile or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Obtain Board approval before moving, adding, modifying, removing or replacing any secondary engineering control, and file the 247 CMR 6.15(4) submissions with an application to remodel or to change the configuration or square footage.
Apply at least 90 days before the desired relocation date and wait for Board approval before relocating.

Apply to modify the registration for a new name or address, and on a transfer of the business with its controlled substances give the Special Agent in Charge at least 14 days' advance notice; on a discontinuance without a transfer, return the certificate of registration and any unexecuted order forms for cancellation.

Decide, in its discretion and on the listed factors, whether an applicant, licensee or interest holder is suitable to establish or maintain a pharmacy, and whether a proposed Manager of Record is suitable to manage one.

common_traps.text: Importing the 14-day notice clock into a relocation or a remodel. Both are approvals with an express prohibition on acting first, and 247 CMR 6.16 sets 90 days while 247 CMR 6.15 sets no day count at all.
Reading the heading of 247 CMR 6.12, Notifications, as covering every change to a pharmacy. The only change it reaches is the name under which the pharmacy operates.
Treating a rebrand as cosmetic because the licence holder, the premises and the ownership are all unchanged, and reporting it at the next renewal.

Treating the buyer's application as discharging the seller's notice, or stopping at that notice when 247 CMR 6.11(1) also sends the outgoing licensee to the provisions on closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances.

Forgetting that the stock has a procedure of its own. 247 CMR 6.14 adds a certified notice, a 14-day wait, a dual-signed transfer-date inventory, a ten-day attestation from both pharmacies and a bar on the transferor holding anything afterwards.

Believing that filing the remodel application is itself the permission, so that work may begin while the application is pending, and submitting drawings without the counseling area or the transport security plan.

Reading 247 CMR 6.15(3) as the whole filing for a compounding pharmacy. 247 CMR 6.15(4) adds certified blueprints with ISO classifications, a containment strategy, an environmental monitoring plan, a re-certification plan and a continuity of care plan, and 247 CMR 6.15(2) separately bars touching a secondary engineering control before approval.
Using the staff-pharmacist substitution for an outgoing Manager of Record who is merely unwilling, or omitting reportable Schedule VI substances from the inventory behind the attestation.

Reading the silence of 247 CMR 6.10 as meaning a change of Manager of Record has no deadline. 247 CMR 20.05(1) gives the pharmacy 14 calendar days from the resignation, termination or change, and 247 CMR 20.05(3) gives the departing manager the same period for a notice of his or her own.
Overlooking the longer clock that follows a change of owner or manager at some pharmacies: 247 CMR 20.06(6)(e) and 247 CMR 20.07(2) require a report within 30 days.
Reading the 247 CMR 6.03 factors as reaching only the named applicant and only Massachusetts pharmacy history, or assuming every listed factor describes misconduct.

Sending every question about the Board's discretion to 247 CMR 6.03. A change-of-Manager-of-Record application is decided on 247 CMR 6.10(3), which adds discipline by the Board within five years and has no prescriptive-privileges factor.

Treating the Massachusetts filings as the whole answer on a sale or a move. 21 CFR 1301.52 bars the assignment of a DEA registration and sets its own 14-day notice to the Special Agent in Charge, and 21 CFR 1301.51 governs a change of name or address.
